title: cislunar-custody: Custody horizons for ground-based angles-only tracking of cislunar periodic orbits
description:
Python code, data and manuscript for a study of how long an object on a cislunar periodic orbit can go unobserved before it leaves a ground-based telescope search pattern (the custody horizon).

Contents: Earth–Moon CR3BP orbit catalogue (L1/L2 halo, 9:2 NRHO, Lyapunov, DRO); ground optical sensor and visibility model (four sites, Moon exclusion, Krisciunas–Schaefer moonlight, photometry); Cramér–Rao bounds; EKF, UKF, Gaussian-mixture UKF and particle filters; linear, unscented and Monte Carlo gap propagation; a JPL DE440 ephemeris + solar radiation pressure cross-check with multiple-shooting orbit counterparts; 47 unit tests and scripts that regenerate every figure.

Key results: cislunar targets sit 4–14° from the Moon, causing an unavoidable 8.5–16 day lunar-phase blackout; the custody horizon exceeds 30 days for the NRHO and DRO and is 11–17 days for the unstable L1 halo and L2 Lyapunov orbits, set mainly by the tracking-arc length before the gap; the unscented transform of the post-fit covariance predicts the horizon (log-R² = 1.00) while the orbit's FTLE alone does not; linear (EKF-style) prediction gives false custody after about one week on unstable orbits.
